title: The axiom of choice: choice functions, well-ordering, and Zorn’s lemma

based_on.title: Axiomatic Set Theory
based_on.pages: 100–101, 117–121 (Theorem 5.14, Definition 5.15, and Theorem 7.5, comparability, Tukey, and Hausdorff equivalents)

summary: Equivalent selection, comparison, and maximality principles, with Hartogs’s theorem and the first uncountable ordinal.
abstract: Choosing one member of each nonempty subset of the natural numbers is easy: take its least member. The axiom of choice asserts that simultaneous selections also exist for arbitrary families of nonempty sets, even when no rule has been given. This is equivalent to saying that every set can be well-ordered, so every nonempty subset has a first element. Another equivalent form, Zorn’s lemma, guarantees a maximal element whenever every chain in a nonempty partially ordered set has an upper bound. Here a chain consists of pairwise comparable elements, and maximal means that no strictly larger element exists.
